court-45.claim: The Delhi High Court closed a petition by two electors whose names were left off Delhi's roll after they moved house and could not fill the enumeration form. They had asked the Court to quash para 4(c) of the SIR guidelines and to change the procedure that requires such electors to seek fresh inclusion through Form 6, and to restore their entries and let them move them to their new address through Form 8. The Commission's standing counsel said they could file Form 6 and that the Electoral Registration Officer would help. The first petitioner said that filing Form 6 would be a false declaration. The bench said that, since the suggestion came from the Commission's counsel on the officer's instructions, his fear of being accused of a false declaration was misplaced. It closed the petition and said the petitioners could file Form 6 if they wished, to be processed in accordance with law. It did not decide the challenge to the guidelines.

court-58.claim: In Hemtabad, a seat reserved for Scheduled Castes in Uttar Dinajpur district, the Election Commission has filed appeals against 15,381 of the 34,327 electors whom judicial officers examined and found eligible, 44.8%, The Wire reported. Of the 13,776 pending appeals, 12,758 carry the code that activists read, and The Wire says it verified, as the batch lodged on the evening of 5 April 2026, 978 carry the code for 6 April, and 40 were filed online. The paper reported that 599 of the appeals with the 5 April code concern electors cleared in the constituency's twelfth and last supplementary list, which was published on 6 April, so the appeals were on record before the list that cleared those electors was made public. The 599 come from nine polling stations, and 162 of them from part 237. Of the 2,65,162 electors on Hemtabad's draft roll, 52,542 were placed under adjudication, and judicial officers struck 18,215 off the roll and found 34,327 eligible. By The Wire's classification of names, which counts the elector's own name or a relative's, at least 97.7% of the electors appealed against have Muslim names, as do all 599, and at least 97% of all those the judges cleared do, so the appeals largely mirror who was cleared. court-65.claim: The Wire's classification of the names in appeal records compiled by the Civic Research Group finds that at least 14,39,797 of the 16,08,175 electors against whose inclusion the Election Commission has appealed, after judicial officers examined them and found them eligible, have Muslim names, 89.5%. In every group the Commission appealed against between 46.5% and 51.2% of the electors the judges cleared, and the report says that across seats there is almost no relationship between a seat's Muslim share and the share of its cleared electors appealed against. It counts 137 constituencies where at least 90% of the electors appealed against have Muslim names, and 2,62,416 electors with Muslim names facing appeals in the 160 seats where Muslims are under a fifth of the population. court-66.claim: Residents of Maharashtra filed a writ petition before the Kolhapur Bench of the Bombay High Court through the advocate Asim Sarode asking it to quash 14 administrative orders passed by the Election Commission and the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, over the past ten months, Bar and Bench reported on 24 September. The petition relies on The Indian Express's report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to these decisions on at least 14 occasions, and says the objections concerned voter registration, deletion and restoration of names, the electoral roll database, the functioning of registration officers and software. It argues that the Commission did not act in accordance with section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, and that the Chief Election Commissioner failed to discharge his duties faithfully, so that no protection can extend to his actions in office. It also challenges the changes made to Form 6 in July. It asks for the 14 orders to be quashed, for the revision in Maharashtra to be stayed, for every elector deleted in Maharashtra in the revision to be restored, for the Assembly elections due in the states where the revision was held to be postponed until rolls are prepared in accordance with law, and for a judicial committee headed by a retired High Court judge to inquire into the deletions and the blockages in the software. On 28 September a bench of Justices Sharmila Deshmukh and Neeraj Dhote declined Sarode's request to hear it that day or the next and listed it for 22 October, Bar and Bench reported. The bench asked what was urgent about it and what private right the petitioners held against the Commission, and Sarode replied that the petition was filed for voters who feel their rights are being infringed. No report of a hearing on 22 October or of any later order was found.

court-69.claim: The First Additional Sessions Judge, Sujit Kumar, on 30 October rejected the Banbhoolpura police's application to stay a Haldwani magistrate's order of 6 October to register an FIR over Form 7s seeking the deletion of 28 electors (form7-36), Dainik Jagran and Live Hindustan reported on 11 November. The station house officer of Banbhoolpura had filed a revision petition against the order and asked for it to be stayed. The court held that the police are not a victim or an aggrieved party in the matter and that registering an FIR and investigating on information of a cognisable offence is their legal duty, Dainik Jagran reported. By the account of the complainant's advocate, Manish Kumar Pandey, the court also questioned why no FIR had been registered for about 24 days. The revision petition is listed for 7 December 2026, and with the stay refused the magistrate's order stands. The complainant, a resident of Indiranagar who says he is the BJP's booth level agent, alleges that an unknown person misused his identity and login to file the Form 7s online on 12 August 2026 against electors of part 134, that he learnt of it on 20 August, and that he neither filed them nor authorised anyone to. Live Hindustan reports that the order of 6 October was passed by the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Shubhangi Gupta. It also reports the complainant's account that he went to Delhi on 30 October and raised the case with more than 20 MPs and senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, among them Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi, P. Chidambaram, Mahua Moitra and Mehbooba Mufti.
court-69.response: The Nainital Senior Superintendent of Police, Manjunath T.C., told Live Hindustan that the police were examining the legal aspects of the case. The complainant's advocate told Dainik Jagran that no FIR had yet been registered and called that a serious matter. Neither report gives the police's grounds for the revision petition. Live Hindustan says the allegations have not been confirmed and that the investigation of the forms, user IDs and login records on the Commission's portal could show who filed them. The police had told the magistrate that the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer (form7-36).
